title: Collections Desk Guide: Subsequent-Return Charge on Retail Installment Contracts
content:
**Rule.** A returned-payment fee on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts carries a subsequent-return charge counted from the contract's other fee-bearing returns in the rolling 12 months:

- two or more other fee-bearing returns: adds **10.00**;
- exactly one: adds **5.00**;
- none: adds nothing.

**What is counted.** Returns on the same contract whose return reason is insufficient funds, account closed, stop payment or uncollected funds, dated in the rolling 12 months ending on the day the fee is worked out — records dated later than the same calendar day 12 months before that day (the last day of that month when that day does not exist) and on or before it — other than the return being charged. Returns for an unauthorized debit or a bank error are not counted.

| Other fee-bearing returns in the rolling 12 months | Subsequent-return charge |
|---|---|
| 0 | nothing |
| 1 | 5.00 |
| 2 | 10.00 |
| 3 or more | 10.00 |

**Hypothetical history.** Today's return for insufficient funds is charged. Earlier, the contract had a stop-payment return four months ago, a bank-error return two months ago, and an uncollected-funds return fourteen months ago. Only the stop-payment return counts — the bank-error return is not fee-bearing and the other is outside the window — so 5.00 is added.
